agent.title: Control machine
agent.subtitle: Let one always-on server own the schedules for every database and container backup
agent.uninstalled: Agent removed; backups it owned now run on this machine again
agent.uninstallConfirm: This stops the service and removes the unit and the binary. Bundles and records stay in /var/lib/deploycode. Configs handed to it fall back to this machine so one side always runs them.
agent.syncStale: The copy on the control machine differs from this one - push the config again.
agent.pickHint: Pick an always-on Linux server. Once installed it backs up every server over SSH, including itself.
agent.binaryHint: Shipped inside the installer - press Install / update and the client pushes it to the control machine. No build step needed.
agent.binaryMissingHint: This client build has no agent binary inside (likely an older installer). Reinstall the latest build, or put a compiled deploy-agent into <data dir>/agent/ and restart.
agent.portless: No listening ports at all: install, push, run and read-back are each one SSH session started by the client.
agent.noServersHint: The control machine is a server too - add one on the Servers page first.
agent.notInstalledHint: Pick the control machine and press Install / update: the client uploads the agent, writes the systemd unit and pushes the config once.
agent.metricClockHint: Schedule times are read in this timezone; the client converts yours when the two differ.
agent.metricDiskHint: Floor {{floor}}: no new backup job starts below it.
agent.metricBundlesHint: Bundles live only on the control machine and rotate by their keep counts.
agent.diskLowWarning: Free space is below the floor, so the control machine refuses new backup jobs. Clean the bundle directory or lower the keep count.
agent.serviceDownWarning: The resident deploy-agent service on the control machine is not running under systemd (inactive / failed): the config still reads back, but nothing will fire on schedule. Run systemctl status deploy-agent and journalctl -u deploy-agent there, then systemctl start deploy-agent.
agent.scheduleShifted: You set {{local}} locally; the control machine runs it at {{agent}} its own time (different timezones).
agent.ownedTitle: Configs handed to the control machine
agent.ownedHint: The control machine runs these schedules. Press Push config after editing, or its copy stays on the old version.
agent.staleNotice: Schedule changes were not pushed: {{detail}}. The control machine still runs the previous copy.
agent.strandedNotice: The control machine still holds configs this machine no longer hands over: {{detail}}. Both will run tonight; press Push config to revoke them.
agent.staleScheduleBackup: Scheduled backup changes have not been pushed, so the control machine still has the previous copy (toggle, time and selected config all count).
agent.staleScheduleContainer: Scheduled container backup changes have not been pushed, so the control machine still has the previous copy (toggle, time and checked configs all count).
agent.stragglerList: The control machine still holds: {{names}}. On this machine they are back to local or deleted; without another push it keeps running them every night.
agent.recordsIntro: These records live on the control machine and are listed separately: deleting local ones does not touch them.
agent.recordsFootnote: Sizes and durations come from the control machine, which also keeps the bundles.
agent.logsIntro: Reads the agents own journald log: scheduling, yields and why a run failed.
agent.dangerHint: Removing the agent only stops the service and deletes the binary; bundles and records stay on the control machine.
agent.orphanHint: These machines had the agent installed and were handed work, but switching control machines failed to reclaim them. They still run their schedule from their own copy, which keeps every server's plaintext credentials. Reclaim them one by one.
agent.reclaimDone: Agent reclaimed on the old control machine
